title: The Loyacano house, Glenn Miller visit and Joe Loyacano's saxophone
summary: Sal talks about Mr. Loyacano's house where touring bandleaders ate, Joe's saxophone playing, and meeting Glenn Miller.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Who's the people you said used to go eat dinner at Lycanna's? Some of them.

Oh, well, that was a big shot. It was after. The best, man. Next to my house, Mr. Lycanna, man. If I was saying the wrong thing, I would say because it was being taped, see. I'd have to stick myself. So, Mr. Joe and I, Mr. Lloyd Cannon, the old man, Lloyd Cannon. I worked with good buddies, you know. I could understand the old man better than his own son, man. He was getting mad at Steve. It was a big shot. He was going on the tape, singing the theater, you know. Mr. Joe said, come on, Salvatore. Go in the back, man. These macaroni, little vino, you know. Mr. Joe, you know. Steve coming in between, in the missions, sanguins, tuxedo pants, suspenders, you know. Big deal, you know. So, and that house right there where you've been, the other day, like two weeks ago. Glenn Miller came there. Jack Teagarden, Vito Musso, all the best. When they come in town, they come there. Quaglina, the tobacco man, Italian to Italian.
He did that when he started.
He brought, I don't know, it's called the little box of gals, you know.

Well, wait a minute. This is before, way back. I'm going to go back when. Coming around there, Mr. Quaglina, had Philip, trombones playing. Joe played saxophone, and he played trombones. Years later, it was the little parody, man. You're talking about. But now, I come around there. And boy, they knew that Joe was the top saxophone player. Joe had a beautiful tone. See, Joe played violin for us. He knew music back, but he played saxophone from Warren Ries in high school, who played saxophone. Every day, he practiced on the scales, see. That's all he needed. When he got the other deal, he had the tone for Ries, see. Castor Caressor, I got him one day to play Rosa Piccadilly on the stage, it was going to be a little bit more, man. I brought Charlie Scaggaleone, Joe was first, man, on the stage, see. Joe was great. So anyhow, Joe was playing saxophone later, see, playing all the big bands you're talking about. So when the band came in town, Smith-Bullow, you know, Smith-Bullow, good looking guy, couldn't play, couldn't sing good. And the band lead up, like, the other, and then he's the rockiest band. I used to go with Joe up there, with the band, see. The Glenn Miller story, saw on the radio, on the picture. I saw that in reality, with the clarinet, that hard note there, man. Glenn, just come off, Papermans go up there, want you hear Glenn? I go up to the club for us, you see. Glenn was on the show's sleeve, you know, with the baritone lead, the band. One time I was on Canal Street, man, check him to try for WPA, man, me. He'll come there with Glenn Miller, man, he stopped by there by me, man. He said, this is a good job you're doing there. I said, yeah, I'm checking all the drunks here. I'm on the book here, because of the blue room. Glenn Miller, he said, yeah, I'm over there, not the blue room, you know. He said, tell me the band, you know. I said, thank you, man, fine. I got a table here for me, you know. I said, no, I don't want to tell you, so I'm on the drunks. I thought it was nuts, man. So I woke up and I said, man, blah, blah, blah, blah, Miller, man. In the band there, Harry James, boy. Sterling Bowes, remember Bowes? I never knew him. He left town before I came here. He died, I played with Bowes, played trumpet, see. He looked like strictly Joe Collins, man. Sharp, little glasses, but I played a fine horn, man. He died, and he was from Alabama, you know. He died after playing piano, man, TB, man. He killed himself when he found that TB. But he started with Bowes. He was in the band.
